title: Reaching Lyra
teaches: transfer windows — the target has to be somewhere else when you leave
brief:
Lyra is twelve thousand kilometres out and takes nearly thirty-eight hours to go round. A transfer from your orbit takes seven and a quarter hours, during which Lyra moves seventy degrees.

So you do not aim at Lyra. You aim at where Lyra will be — which means leaving when it is about 110 degrees ahead of you, and not a moment else. Windows come round every thirty-nine minutes.

Get inside Lyra's sphere of influence. The SOI sensor will read 1 when you are.
hints: TGTA is the heading toward Lyra. RAD is the heading straight up, which is also where you are in your own orbit. The difference between them is the phase angle.
Wait until that difference is about 110 degrees, then burn prograde until APO reaches Lyra's orbit — 12 000 km.
Put a WAIT inside your polling loop. It costs nothing and lets the simulation skip ahead between checks.

reference.solution:
; Reaching Lyra — wait for the window, then one long prograde burn.
        ORIENT  PROGRADE
window: WAIT    2
        SET     R0, TGTA
        SUB     R0, RAD
        IF      R0 < 0
        ADD     R0, 360
        IF      R0 > 112
        JMP     window
        IF      R0 < 108
        JMP     window
        THROTTLE 1
        BURN    UNTIL APO > 11900000
        THROTTLE 0
        WAIT    UNTIL SOI >= 1
        HALT
